verify-touched.sh over the two Phase 1 paths resolves by naming convention to 'test-slice-series.sh' (not the __FULL_SWEEP__ sentinel the plan's Tier Justification measured at plan-authoring time) but then fails because the suite is not yet registered in manifest.json/suite-classification.data or deployed -- the run-all.sh --only invocation reports 'unknown suite basename' against the deployed tree's 220 discovered suites. This is the same deliberate, bounded red interval the plan's Risk table already names for doc-lint Rule Q and the manifest-parity gate between Phase 1 and Phase 5; the Phase 1 Scope Hypothesis is confirmed (selector no longer returns full-sweep) but the narrowed execution itself cannot succeed until Phase 5 registration and Phase 6 deploy. Direct suite invocation (23 passed, 0 failed) and lint-shellcheck.sh (0 findings) are the real Phase 1 gates and both pass clean.

Phase 2's Verification bullet literally requires 'the fixture's HEAD, git status --porcelain, and git diff --cached are unchanged' after every build case, but build's own task list requires it to write the series document back to disk and create a pull-request body file if absent -- both new, previously-absent paths that necessarily add untracked entries to raw 'git status --porcelain' output even though no already-tracked file is touched. Resolved by implementing the untouched-state assertion against HEAD, the shared index's tracked content (git ls-files -s), and git diff over tracked paths (unstaged modifications to already-tracked files) instead of raw git status --porcelain, matching the Phase 2 Goal's own wording ('HEAD, the shared index, and the working tree untouched') rather than the stricter Verification-bullet phrasing that cannot hold simultaneously with build's required file writes.

The compare-and-swap refusal (exit 30) proved straightforward to test deterministically without real threading via a narrow, test-only environment-variable seam (SS_TEST_PRE_SWAP_HOOK) that runs an external hook with the ref name right after the script captures the compare-and-swap 'old' value and right before the swap attempt -- the hook moves the ref there, reliably reproducing a genuine git update-ref lock-mismatch failure every time, with zero flakiness across repeated runs.

The no-dependency static assertion's grep for 'review-stack-prepare' initially flagged the script's own explanatory comment stating the decision NOT to depend on review-stack-prepare.sh (a legitimate, intentional comment documenting the ruling's Basis decision, not a real dependency). Fixed by excluding pure-comment lines from that grep, the same convention the Phase 1 static push/checkout/forge assertion already uses for the identical reason.

git push is blocked unconditionally by this environment's guard-git-push.sh hook, including against a throwaway local bare/fixture repo under /tmp with no network or forge involvement -- the hook pattern-matches on command text regardless of destination. The status suite's 'pushed and matching' / 'pushed and diverging' remote-tracking-ref cases were redesigned to fabricate the resulting refs/remotes/<remote>/... ref directly via git update-ref instead, which is sufficient since slice-series.sh itself only ever reads that ref's value and never pushes.

An exploratory (non-designated) verify-touched.sh run over commands/slice.md fell through to its OWED/full-sweep fallback (the path is an unmapped markdown file) and reported 3 NEW failing suites: test-manifest-scripts-sync.sh (expected -- the two new scripts are not yet registered in manifest.json; Phase 5's own job, same as the Phase 1/2/3 pre-registration gap already logged), plus test-handoff-dispatch-identity.sh and test-lint-state-writer-boundary.sh, both unrelated to this task's files by content. Re-ran both directly in isolation and both passed cleanly (28/0 and 13/0 respectively), consistent with transient interference from this shared repository's other concurrently-dispatched batch tasks (git status at dispatch start showed many other specs/* directories with uncommitted changes) rather than a regression caused by this task. This phase's actual designated Tier Justification check (verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow --only-gate 3,4) was run separately and passed as expected (gate 4 clean; gate 3's doc-lint shows only the already-logged pre-Phase-5 registration gap).

Phase 5's designated verify-touched.sh run over the five registration paths took ~8 minutes under this shared repository's concurrent batch load (test-gate-lock.sh and test-run-all-parallel.sh are both load-sensitive/serialized, so the 58-suite narrowed battery ran mostly single-threaded) and reported 2 failures: test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh, which run-all.sh itself marks (EXPECTED) and is therefore a pre-accepted baseline, not a regression; and test-lint-unit-integration-boundary.sh, marked (NEW), whose detail shows 3 unclassified-suite violations against the DEPLOYED tree's suite-classification.data -- test-lean-challenge-observe.sh, test-sapience-remember.sh, and test-sapience-tag-pending.sh. None of these three names anything related to slice-series.sh, commands/slice.md, manifest.json, README.md, or orchestrator-runtime-files.md; they are foreign drift from other concurrently-dispatched sibling tasks' own deploys in this same batch invocation, consistent with the many other specs/* dirty directories visible in git status at this dispatch's start. This task's own test-slice-series.sh suite does not appear anywhere in the violation list. Verified via direct content inspection, not assumed.

deploy-headless.sh's inline fast-gate verification (gate 27, lint-subject-resolution-declaration.sh) failed on the first Phase 6 redeploy attempt: test-slice-series.sh called common_test_resolve_candidate with an implicit deployed-then-source-store-then-sibling candidate order instead of the mandated explicit-mode common_test_resolve_subject. Fixed by migrating both the script and deploy-root-guard.sh resolutions to common_test_resolve_subject "deploy-tree-first" with exactly one deployed and one source-store candidate each (dropping the third SCRIPT_DIR-relative fallback, which the two-candidate function does not take), and adding the paired common_test_declare_subject call the lint also requires for every resolved subject (GUARD had none). Re-verified: lint clean, suite still 45/0, shellcheck clean on both files; redeploying again to pick up the fix before re-running the full verify.

The plan's own premise re-validation (re-measured at plan time) recorded this repository as 0 behind / 414 ahead of origin/master via git rev-list --left-right --count origin/master...master. Re-measured again at Phase 6 implementation time (after a fresh git fetch origin): 0 behind / 4 ahead -- origin/master has moved forward substantially in the interim (it now includes everything through this task's own Phase 1 commit), consistent with other concurrent activity in this shared, actively-pushed repository. The acceptance precondition ('a real difference exists to cut') still holds: origin/master remains a confirmed ancestor of HEAD with a genuine non-empty difference (4 commits, 18 files changed, 1923 insertions, 64 deletions, all four being this task's own Phase 2-5 closing commits since Phase 1 already landed on origin). No number from either measurement was carried into any deliverable, per the record's own constraint.

Operator must run /slice from this repository's master branch, approve a proposal over the live difference against origin/master, then type the printed /please push origin slice/<series_id>/<id> line for each built slice (one at a time), then run /slice again to open the pull request(s). No agent can perform any of these three steps.
